subject: ventures/deploy-concurrency-check
professional: a senior DevOps / release engineer who owns GitHub Actions deploy pipelines; they check first that the tool's model of `concurrency` matches GitHub's documented semantics (workflow- and job-level groups both apply, group names are case-insensitive, one running + one pending per group with the pending replaced, `queue: max` FIFO, `cancel-in-progress` as an expression) and that it is quiet on their real repository

evidence.correctness: Ran check.py on 10 hand-written probes and on this repo's 137 .github/workflows files. Canonical cases are right: priv-portfolio-pages.yml (group portfolio-pages-${{ github.ref }}, cancel false) is clean, a head_ref||run_id group on a push deploy is flagged per-run, ref: main is flagged. Departures from GitHub's docs (docs.github.com 'Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs', fetched 2026-11-26): (a) a stable workflow-level group 'deploy-production' plus a job-level 'job-${{ github.sha }}' is reported HIGH 'serializes nothing' although the workflow-level group still serializes whole runs (classify.mjs:308 uses job ?? workflow instead of both); (b) jobs with groups 'deploy-Prod' and 'deploy-prod' are reported split, but the docs say 'The concurrency group name is case insensitive'; (c) group deploy-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }} is not flagged (context missing from PER_RUN_CONTEXTS); (d) two workflows each with group '${{ github.workflow }}-prod' on environment production are not flagged although they resolve to different groups (c1-prod, c2-prod) - the cross-file comparison is on unresolved expression strings; (e) flow mapping 'concurrency: { group: deploy-prod, cancel-in-progress: true }' and (f) cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }} both pass silently. On this repo all 12 findings hang off environments used as secret scopes (publish, paid-agents) or credential scopes; I judge at most 1-2 (priv-cloudflare-email no concurrency) to be races a release engineer would act on.
evidence.completeness: All five README checks fire on their fixtures; CLI flags --json, --fail-on-risk, directory scan and cross-file split all work (12 findings across 137 files, exit codes tested). README test command `node --test 'ventures/deploy-concurrency-check/**/*.test.mjs'` from repo root runs 44/44. Page and two articles ship and are in the sitemap. No suppression/allowlist mechanism for an accepted race, which the page itself says a team may decide.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 44 pass, 0 fail (293 ms). Seven seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: six caught (remove github.run_id / github.event.after from per-run list, exempt ref main, split threshold >2, cross-file threshold <3, check.py cancel == 'yes' - parity test catches JS/Python drift); one survived (dropping 'ship' from DEPLOY_WORD_RE). The parity test is strong. But the tests encode the same semantic gaps as the code: no test for case-insensitive groups, nested workflow+job groups, flow-mapping concurrency or expression cancel-in-progress; page.test 'no page loads anything over the network' checks the source file, not the served page that gets a beacon injected.
evidence.craft: Read classify.mjs (518 lines) and check.py (615 lines). Clear, commented, deliberate indentation scan, stable finding ids, escaping of pasted input tested. Defects: flow-style mappings misparsed silently (whole '{...}' taken as the group name, classify.mjs:132); jobBodyIndent recomputed inside the per-line loop (quadratic, harmless at workflow size); cancel-in-progress only matched as literal 'true' with no 'not decidable' note, unlike the ref check which documents its skip of expressions.
evidence.claims: Served page https://marisstella.app/deploy-concurrency-check/ loads ../pf-site.js, ../pf-embed.js and https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js (curl, 2026-11-26), but the footer (index.html:186-188) and README Privacy (README.md:95) say it 'embeds no third-party script, font or analytics service, and makes no network request at all once it has loaded'; the page's own FAQ (index.html:162) contradicts the footer by mentioning cookieless analytics. Licence: LICENSE is FSL-1.1-MIT and the tool page says so, but README.md:101 says 'MIT (see LICENSE)' and vs-reading-your-workflows-yourself.html:146 says 'The CLI is MIT licensed'. Article how-a-deploy-ships-an-older-commit.html:101 says runs in one group 'apply in the order they were queued'; the docs say a newer pending run cancels and replaces the existing pending one, and FIFO 'ordering is not guaranteed'. The run-log claim (article :186) is overstated: actions/checkout logs the resolved commit SHA. vs page :88 says a scan compares group strings 'perfectly' while it compares unresolved, case-sensitive expressions. README '35 assertions' is stale (44 tests). llms.txt carries 'estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial' boilerplate that does not fit a workflow scanner. Good: disclaimer, no-warranty, not-affiliated and limits sections are present and honest about what a clean report means.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: scan my repo's workflows in CI with --fail-on-risk. On this repository it would fail the build on 10 HIGH findings, nearly all from environments used to scope secrets (README rule 1 treats any environment: as deploying), with no way to accept or suppress one. A release engineer would either drop --fail-on-risk or stop reading findings, which the README itself names as the failure to avoid. In the browser, a single file paste works well and the explanations are excellent.
evidence.domain: Compared against GitHub's concurrency documentation. Right: no group = parallel runs; per-run keys defeat the group; cancel-in-progress on a deploy is a partial-write hazard; split groups per target; pin checkout to github.sha. Departs: treats job-level concurrency as replacing workflow-level (both apply); ignores case-insensitivity of group names; does not know `queue: max` (FIFO, 'ordering is not guaranteed') or the default pending-replacement rule; ignores cancel-in-progress expressions; equates 'environment' with 'deploy target' although environments are widely used purely as secret/approval scopes.

checks.what: workflow-level stable group plus job-level per-run group on a deploy job
checks.method: GitHub docs, Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs: workflow-level concurrency limits runs of the workflow in that group; a job-level group is an additional constraint
checks.expected: no per-run finding (whole runs serialized by deploy-production)

checks.what: two jobs on environment production with groups deploy-Prod and deploy-prod
checks.method: GitHub docs: 'The concurrency group name is case insensitive'

checks.what: group deploy-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }} on a workflow_run-triggered deploy
checks.method: GitHub docs, workflow_run event payload: head_sha is the triggering run's commit, different on every run

checks.what: two workflows (c1, c2) each with group ${{ github.workflow }}-prod deploying environment production
checks.method: hand evaluation of the expression: resolves to c1-prod and c2-prod, two groups, so no serialization (docs: a group only serializes runs that share it)
checks.observed: No deployment race found in 2 file(s), exit 0

checks.what: push-triggered deploy with group ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}, cancel true, checkout ref: main
checks.method: GitHub docs head_ref||run_id example: head_ref is undefined on push, so the group falls back to the run ID, unique per run
checks.expected: per-run HIGH, cancel-in-progress MEDIUM, mutable-ref MEDIUM

checks.what: this repo's priv-portfolio-pages.yml (group portfolio-pages-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress false)
checks.method: GitHub docs: github.ref is stable across pushes to main, so runs queue

checks.what: flow-mapping concurrency { group: deploy-prod, cancel-in-progress: true } on a deploy
checks.method: YAML 1.2 flow mapping; GitHub docs cancel-in-progress semantics

checks.what: cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }} on a push-to-main deploy
checks.method: GitHub docs: cancel-in-progress may be an expression; on main it evaluates true
checks.expected: a finding or an explicit 'not decidable' note

checks.what: footer/README: no third-party script or analytics, no network request after load
checks.expected: only inline/module scripts from the product

checks.method: head LICENSE vs README.md:101, vs page :146, index.html:202
checks.observed: LICENSE and index say FSL-1.1-MIT; README and vs page say MIT

checks.what: article: runs sharing a group 'apply in the order they were queued'
checks.method: GitHub docs: default queue single cancels and replaces the existing pending run; FIFO ordering 'not guaranteed'
checks.expected: newest pending run replaces older pending ones
checks.observed: claims every run applies in queue order
present; limits section honest that a clean report is not 'safe'
none left; but llms.txt line 5 carries 'estimates from the numbers typed in' boilerplate

checks.what: run on this repository's 137 workflows as a CI gate
checks.method: hand review of each finding's environment
checks.expected: findings a release engineer would act on
checks.observed: 12 findings (10 HIGH), almost all on secret-scope environments publish/paid-agents; at most 1-2 actionable

defects.what: Privacy claim false on the served page: footer and README say no third-party script or analytics and no network request after load, but the deployed page loads static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js, pf-site.js and pf-embed.js; the FAQ at index.html:162 contradicts the footer. page.test.mjs checks the source, not what ships.

Job-level concurrency is treated as replacing workflow-level (job ?? workflow), so a stable workflow-level group with a per-run job-level group is reported HIGH 'serializes nothing'; GitHub applies both, and the workflow group serializes the runs.

Split-group comparison is on raw expression strings: case-sensitive although GitHub group names are case-insensitive (false HIGH on deploy-Prod vs deploy-prod), and blind to expressions that resolve differently per file (${{ github.workflow }}-prod in two files is not flagged).
Licence misstated: LICENSE is FSL-1.1-MIT but README says 'MIT (see LICENSE)' and the comparison page says 'The CLI is MIT licensed'.

Any `environment:` makes a job 'deploying'; environments used only to scope secrets produce HIGH findings (10 of 12 on this repo's workflows), and there is no way to suppress an accepted finding, so --fail-on-risk is unusable on such a repo.

Silent false negatives: flow-mapping `concurrency: { group: ..., cancel-in-progress: true }` is read as a group named '{ ... }'; `cancel-in-progress: ${{ expr }}` is ignored with no 'not decidable' note; github.event.workflow_run.head_sha / workflow_run.id are missing from PER_RUN_CONTEXTS.

Article says runs sharing a group 'apply in the order they were queued'; GitHub cancels and replaces the pending run when a newer one arrives (intermediate commits never deploy) and FIFO ordering under queue: max is 'not guaranteed'. `queue: max` is not modelled anywhere.
Article/FAQ say the run log records the ref, not the resolved commit; actions/checkout logs the checked-out SHA.
README says '35 assertions'; the suite has 44 tests.
llms.txt carries 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial' boilerplate that does not describe a workflow scanner.
Seeded mutant removing 'ship' from DEPLOY_WORD_RE survives: the documented name-based deploy signal is only partly tested.

verdict: A well-written, well-tested scanner (44/44 tests, 6 of 7 seeded mutants caught, a JS/Python parity test) whose five patterns are right on the canonical cases, but which does not meet the bar. Its model of GitHub concurrency departs from the documentation in ways a release engineer hits quickly: workflow- and job-level groups are treated as either/or (false HIGH), group names are compared case-sensitively and unresolved (false HIGH and a missed cross-file split), flow mappings and expression cancel-in-progress pass silently, and every secret-scope environment is a 'deploy' (10 HIGH findings on this repo, at most 1-2 actionable, no suppression). Claims fail the gate: the served page loads a Cloudflare analytics beacon and two site scripts while the footer and README promise no third-party script and no network request, and README and the comparison page call an FSL-1.1-MIT licence 'MIT'. Scores: correctness 2, completeness 3, verification 3, craft 3, claims 1, fitness 2, domain 2.
